scope: Current Vault source and production trust gate
Production ClearSign status/catalog and 28 live read-only probes
Production worker-b5 batches matched to live catalog fingerprints
Firmware source for 7.16/7.17 schema and embedded-call support
Verified Relay v3.2 and TychoRouterV3 ABI/source for the reported failed swap

findings.title: The router used by the failed ETH-to-USDT swap has no signed coverage
evidence: Live /v1/evm/schema rejects chain 1, Router v3.2 0x0729e2a4716d9f7dd17858d5d504426d228697f7, selector 0xcd6e13f7, 2180 bytes.
The ERC-7730 endpoint also rejects the outer multicall, both cleanup functions and the Tycho sequentialSwap.
All four production ERC-7730 batch fingerprints match the inspected worker-b5 source; those batches contain no Relay router/depository or Tycho V3 leaves for these addresses.
findings.impact: Existing Relay depository descriptions cannot describe this multicall; AdvancedMode remains required.
findings.remedy: Review and issue four compatible definitions, including every nested call. A root/outer label alone cannot provide full transaction review.

findings.title: Signing new entries alone cannot support the exact incident on current firmware
evidence: The outer calldata is 2180 bytes: canonical ABI 2148 plus a 32-byte suffix.
The Tycho inner calldata is 627 bytes: canonical ABI 612 plus 15 suffix bytes.
Vault erc7730-describe.ts rejects inner arguments not divisible by 32.
Firmware erc7730_workflow_inner_fetchable requires (inner_length - 4) % 32 == 0.
Firmware erc7730_workflow_restore_and_start_calldata explicitly allows trailing bytes only for outer calls.
Firmware 7.16 does not follow embedded-call definitions; Vault gates them at 7.17.0.
findings.impact: Even an authentic signed outer/inner catalog would not make this exact transaction reviewable on 7.16 or current 7.17.
findings.remedy: For a 7.17 implementation, add signed-policy-controlled inner suffix support in both host and firmware, preserving hashing/bounds checks and all suffix bytes; validate exact incident and adversarial mutations. Alternatively implement a bounded dedicated decoder. No upgrade to device firmware was performed.

findings.title: Production catalog publication currently suppresses embedded-call definitions
evidence: worker-b5/worker/shared/erc7730-catalog.ts indexErc7730Catalog skips every program with an embedded-call formatter.
Its reason says Vault never attaches embedded calls, which is stale for the current 7.17 host.
findings.impact: Issuing the outer Relay multicall definition would still leave it unserved under the current publication policy.
findings.remedy: Update and test publication for compatible clients/firmware while retaining the 7.16 rejection in Vault. Do not globally bypass embedded-call checks.

findings.title: Fixed depository coverage is partial despite broader host recognition
evidence: The production catalog has native deposit entries on Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum only.
Native deposit probes on Optimism, BSC, Polygon and Avalanche all return 422.
ERC20 deposit coverage consists of six Base tokens and five Arbitrum tokens. Ethereum USDT deposit returns 422.
findings.impact: A Relay deposit can be understood by the host yet still lack a signed device description.
findings.remedy: New fixed-schema offline catalog entries can close these gaps after chain-specific contract verification and matching Vault schema support. This is separate from the ETH-to-USDT multicall.

findings.title: Solana lookup-table Relay deposits are not supported by the static service
evidence: Bundled native-deposit fixture without an ALT returns VERIFIED.
The ALT fixture returns LOOKUP_TABLES_UNSUPPORTED.
The static worker serves no transaction-bound lookup-table attestation.
findings.impact: A signed Relay instruction schema alone does not resolve lookup-table accounts.
findings.remedy: Resolve the attestation/transport design under the existing offline-signing policy; do not describe arbitrary lookup tables with an instruction label.

findings.title: Depository ClearSign cannot attest destination-chain swap promises
evidence: depositNative encodes depositor and order id plus native value.
depositErc20 encodes depositor, source token, source amount and order id.
Destination chain, final destination address and minimum output are off-chain order terms.
Solana token-deposit schema labels a raw u64 Amount and Vault, not a certified token symbol/decimal identity.
findings.impact: A verified source deposit is not proof of destination delivery or a certified minimum receive amount.
findings.remedy: Keep those limits explicit in the approval card and reports. Review Solana token identity/unit coverage separately.

findings.title: Relay v3.2 migration is newer than the existing deposit coverage model
evidence: Relay documentation announces the v3.2 Router/ApprovalProxy switch on October 26, 2026.
The v3.2 Cancun router is exactly the address in the failed swap.
The older v3 and new v3.2 pairs both remain live during transition.
findings.impact: Coverage must distinguish depository, router versions and approval proxies; the provider name Relay is not a sufficient signing-policy key.
findings.remedy: Track reviewed chain+contract+selector+encoding variants, including approval-proxy transactions and each selected swap provider.
